answer: Policies are written in beacon, settled in lotus, and relic lists every payout. A farm therefore faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 17% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. The attacker spends 35 dollars and 8 days per identity before it can vote at all. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
